data.headline: QQQ: a lower long yield is only one valuation input.
data.summary: The latest ten-year yield supplies a fresh discount-rate reference for technology-heavy equities. It does not tell us whether earnings expectations or equity risk premiums changed. QQQ remains unscored as a trade because independent prices, options and other required signals are missing.

bull.text: The ten-year yield declined from 4.94% on October 30 to 4.91% on November 2. Lower discount rates can support the present value of future cash flows, with other inputs held constant; no QQQ response was collected.

bear.text: SOFR increased from 3.95% to 3.97% on November 3 while the two-year Treasury yield had risen to 4.59% on November 2. The mix does not support treating every funding or valuation benchmark as easing together.

watch.text: Nasdaq mini futures asset managers were net long 65,381 contracts on October 27, down from 77,790 a week earlier. Leveraged funds were net long 2,301. These are related futures categories, not QQQ investor flows.

limitations: Treasury yields describe November 2; SOFR and reverse-repo figures describe November 3. These are delayed official observations, not live prices or the market response to a release.
CFTC figures are October 27 futures-only category positions. Related futures differ from ETF shares and do not identify current purchases, fund flows or individual investors.
Current ETF prices, option chains, gamma, representative social sentiment and dark-pool direction remain independently unmeasured. Hosted displays are separate from saved evidence.
The interpretation describes possible transmission channels, not measured causation, a return prediction or a calibrated trading probability. No prospective model is qualified.
